lead: Eleven parts. Each one ends in something to do, and every check counts towards your points, badges and the class board.

tiles.p1: Four kinds of socialisation, each with a five-question test, and a checklist of twelve things you can say.
tiles.p2: Seven ideas about culture, a quiz on each, and a sorter that puts twenty-one examples into the right idea.
tiles.p3: The family, education, peer groups, the media, religion and the workplace, each with its own activities.
tiles.p4: How sanctions keep us in line, with a sorter that puts sixteen sanctions into formal or informal, positive or negative.
tiles.p5: Seventeen key words on flashcards, with a ten-question quiz drawn from thirty.
tiles.p6: Twenty-six five-mark questions. Build each answer for marks, then write your own and compare it with the model.
tiles.p7: Seven ten-mark questions. Build two paragraphs for marks, then write your own and compare them with the model.
tiles.p8: How the AO2 marks are won, with four items to find the phrase in.
tiles.p9: Where marks are lost and how examiners read an answer, with six answers to judge.
tiles.p10: Your badges, the class board, your progress part by part, today's challenge and this week's mock.
tiles.p11: Seven revision sheets you can read on screen or print.
